inputs: Selected hublist type and optional forceDownload flag.
defaults: forceDownload defaults false; selected index starts at 0; list type starts TYPE_NORMAL; useHttp and running start false.
effects: If HUBLIST_SERVERS has no tokens, refresh returns without events. A selected URL lacking http:// or https:// increments lastServer and returns. With forceDownload=false, a nonempty cache file is parsed first; success fires LoadedFromCache and returns, while cache read failure or empty data falls through to HTTP; a nonempty buffer that fails parsing fires Corrupted and returns without an HTTP request. HTTP starts only when running is false; it clears the selected matrix entry, fires DownloadStarting, and downloads. A concurrent refresh while running does not start another request. HTTP failure removes listener, advances lastServer, clears running and fires DownloadFailed when useHttp. HTTP completion fires DownloadFinished only if parsing succeeds; corrupt parse fires Corrupted. Redirect emits another DownloadStarting.
events: Download start, failure, finish, cache load and corruption listener callbacks.
errors: File cache read exceptions clear the buffer and fall through to HTTP; malformed cache or HTTP payload fires Corrupted. HTTP failure callback carries the failure line. Invalid configured URLs advance selected index without an event.
behavior.completion: HTTP fetch is asynchronous; DownloadFinished occurs only after successful parse. A successful cache parse fires LoadedFromCache and returns synchronously from refresh.
behavior.cancellation: No cancellation contract observed in inspected public manager API.

Given a nonempty cache buffer fails parsing with forceDownload false, then Corrupted fires and refresh returns without HTTP. inputs: Feed URL/name/enabled/update interval; RSS/Atom feed items; ordered feed filters with pattern, match method, action, skipDupes, expiry days, target/group and time-format flag.
preconditions: A feed update task only starts for a non-null feed; timer-driven selection requires allowUpdate(). Filter matching is by item title after trimming spaces and CR/LF; empty and duplicate titles are discarded.
defaults: RSS constructor defaults update interval to 60 minutes, enable=true, lastUpdate=0, dirty=false, token to a generated nonzero value when none supplied; intervals below 10 are clamped to 10. RSSFilter defaults action DOWNLOAD, expiry 3 days, formatTimeParams=false, group empty, and skipDupes=true. Filter action values are DOWNLOAD=0, REMOVE=1, ADD_AUTOSEARCH=2. RSSData dateAdded defaults to current time. (RSSManager.h:39-150)
effects: RSS/Atom parser accepts only new nonempty titles; RSS parser then reads link/pubDate, Atom parser reads href/updated. addData inserts data by title under lock, marks feed dirty, fires RSSDataAdded, then applies filters. REMOVE filters are tested first and matching data is queued for deletion. Remaining filters are considered in order; on a matched skipDupes filter, an existing share or queue duplicate breaks filter evaluation (later filters are not tried). First non-duplicate matching DOWNLOAD or ADD_AUTOSEARCH rule creates an AutoSearch item; DOWNLOAD uses auto-search enabled=true and may search immediately only while max search queue size is below five, ADD_AUTOSEARCH does not. Format-time-params formats target using current time, and the filter expiry is converted from days to an absolute expiration time. downloadFeed updates lastUpdate, queues HttpDownload creation, and feed scheduling allows one update per minute. XML database persistence skips items older than 3 days.
events: RSSDataAdded fires after insertion before filter actions; RSSDataRemoved fires before erasure; RSSDataCleared and feed add/change/remove/update events are emitted by their corresponding operations. A successful or parse-failed nonempty HTTP response still fires RSSFeedUpdated after parsing/catch. An empty response logs status and returns before RSSFeedUpdated.
errors: An empty response logs its HTTP status and produces no RSSFeedUpdated event. XML parse Exception is logged, then RSSFeedUpdated is still fired. Feed retrieval failures are governed by HttpDownload and are not represented by a manager failure listener in this source.
behavior.completion: downloadFeed schedules retrieval on DispatcherQueue; downloadComplete parses on completion callback. Timer-driven feed selection schedules at most one selected feed per minute.
behavior.cancellation: No explicit RSS cancellation operation is exposed; HttpDownload is owned by RSS and replaced/reset by the completion callback.
persistence: Feed metadata/filter data is saved through manager save; RSSData entries are written to RSSDataBase<token>.xml via a temporary file, keeping only entries whose dateAdded is within 3 days.
resources: DispatcherQueue and HttpDownload; RSSManager critical section protects rssList/feed maps/filter mutation; AutoSearchManager, ShareManager and QueueManager are consulted by filter actions.

inputs: Existing AutoSearchPtr and updated item fields; active flag; manual search mode (TYPE_MANUAL_FG/TYPE_MANUAL_BG/TYPE_NORMAL); increment/decrement; finished paths; ordered group list and requested group.
preconditions: Manager methods act on a caller-supplied item; searchItem needs at least one online client hub. A destination group must already exist, except empty string clears a current group.
defaults: AutoSearch default values and constructor time-window defaults are recorded in modules.auto-search.
effects: setItemActive returns false without mutation when state is unchanged. On enabling an expired item it sets expiration to current time plus AUTOSEARCH_EXPIRE_DAYS; if the maximum incremented number was reached it increments maxNumber instead. It changes enabled/status, may schedule an immediate search if due, queues schedule recalculation, and marks the manager dirty. Source uses RLock(cs) around the model mutation.

updateAutoSearch prepares the user matcher and rebuilds pattern, search time/status and excluded patterns under WLock; it queues search-time recalculation, fires ItemUpdated(tab-dirty=true), sets dirty=true, and returns true. clearPaths clears finished path entries under WLock, fires ItemUpdated(tab-dirty=true), and marks dirty.

changeNumber always clears lastError and emits status update; AutoSearch::changeNumber changes curNumber only if useParams and %[inc] are active, resets lastIncFinish and rebuilds pattern. The manager wrapper does not set dirty. searchItem returns false when there are no online hubs; otherwise it delegates to performSearch. TYPE_MANUAL_FG emits SearchForeground directly and sets lastSearch; other types dispatch through SearchManager unless queue overflow prevents it. Manual foreground/background on a disabled item marks it manual.

Group getter returns a copy under read lock; setGroups replaces the list under write lock without event or dirty flag. moveItemToGroup accepts an existing group or empty to clear, emits ItemUpdated(tab-dirty=false), and does not set dirty; invalid names leave the model unchanged.
events: ItemUpdated for update, clear-path, group move, and active/status changes; search events depend on searchItem mode and results.
errors: No hubs causes searchItem=false; invalid group move is ignored. setItemActive=false when requested state equals current.
behavior.completion: Mutations and status/event emission are synchronous. Search dispatch and schedule recalculation use delayed event queue; the actual search/result processing is asynchronous.
behavior.cancellation: No caller cancellation token. Delayed scheduling is manager-owned and search eligibility is rechecked when events run.
persistence: updateAutoSearch, clearPaths and setItemActive mark manager state dirty and the second timer saves after the manager’s 20-second dirty delay. changeNumber and group set/move methods do not mark dirty in their direct implementations; search or other later mutation may persist the shared item.
resources: AutoSearchManager shared mutex, AutoSearch search/group state, online hubs from ClientManager, delayed-event queue and listener speaker.

ownership_evidence: AutoSearchManager receives shared AutoSearchPtr values; it mutates the pointed-to model and serializes manager state in save().
threading_evidence: updateAutoSearch/clearPaths/changeNumber use WLock(cs); setGroups uses WLock and getGroups/hasGroup/getGroupIndex use RLock. setItemActive mutates the AutoSearch under RLock(cs) in the inspected implementation, which is source behavior and a concurrency concern for characterization; moveItemToGroup calls hasGroup under a read lock but its subsequent item mutation/event has no enclosing lock.
records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Expose explicit mutation results and listener snapshots. Preserve no-op/ignored results, group-only dirty-state behavior, and manual foreground/background distinction.
acceptance_scenarios: Given an expired disabled item, when enabling it, then expiration is moved forward by AUTOSEARCH_EXPIRE_DAYS and a recalculation is queued.
Given useParams is false or no %[inc] marker exists, when changeNumber is called, then curNumber is unchanged though the manager wrapper clears the error and emits ItemUpdated.
Given no online hubs, when searchItem is requested, then it returns false without dispatching a search.
Given a group name not in getGroups(), when moveItemToGroup is requested, then the item group remains unchanged and no update is emitted.
Given finished paths, when clearPaths is called, then paths are cleared, ItemUpdated is emitted and the manager is marked dirty.

inputs: Persisted AutoSearch.xml groups, rule fields, finish-path timestamps, associated bundle tokens, dynamic schedule windows, result/search timestamps and bundle completion/error notifications.
preconditions: load runs after settings are available; AutoSearchManager adds its QueueManager listener only after loading to avoid treating restored failed bundles as new duplicate candidates.
defaults: Zero/negative expireTime means no expiry; expiration is reached only when expireTime>0 and <=current time. A maximum number is reached only when parameter incrementation is enabled, maxNumber>0, curNumber>=maxNumber and lastIncFinish=0. Missing SearchDays in saved XML defaults to all seven days; missing start/end time defaults to 00:00 and 23:59; missing target falls back to DOWNLOAD_DIRECTORY. A saved file without Groups restores the default group name “Failed Bundles”. Failed-bundle auto-search candidates expire after 7 days.
effects: Each second the manager checks whether a scheduled search is due and saves dirty XML after at least 20 seconds; each minute checkItems recalculates non-recent priorities, handles post-search increment completion, evaluates expiry/max-number state and search-window boundaries, emits ItemUpdated for schedule/status changes, starts newly enabled work when no next search is pending and recalculates scheduling. Expired searches are removed when REMOVE_EXPIRED_AS is true, disabled when currently enabled otherwise, or have status/event refreshed when already disabled.

Expiration is suppressed while bundles remain associated; once no bundles remain, elapsed expireTime or exceeded max increment marks the item for expiry handling. removePostSearch clears lastIncFinish when AS_DELAY_HOURS is zero or when `lastIncFinish + AS_DELAY_HOURS + 3600 <= current time` (the source uses that exact expression), allowing increment progression; max number prevents further increment and expires the search.

Load restores rule values, group, expiry/timeAdded, search days/window, last search, optional increment params, finished paths and only bundle references that still resolve in QueueManager. Expired rules with no restored bundles are disabled. It recalculates recent and priority status, loads all rules without immediate search, then registers QueueManager listener and resets scheduled times.

addFailedBundle refuses duplicate names and non-release names; accepted rules search the failed bundle directory with exact matching, remove-after-one-hit, FAILED_BUNDLE type, 7-day expiry and AS_FAILED_DEFAULT_GROUP, associate the original bundle and optionally start immediately when it is recent.

resetSearchTimes selects the earlier of normal/recent next ticks and converts it to wall time; maybePopSearchItem returns when not due unless explicitly ignored, when queue overflow exists, or when no hubs are online; otherwise it pops one eligible item under lock and performs one normal search.
events: ItemUpdated when scheduling/status state changes; ItemAdded/ItemRemoved for addFailedBundle expiry handling; ItemSearched when a scheduled search is issued/completes.
errors: load/save are noexcept wrappers around settings XML; individual malformed XML behavior beyond the parsed fields is not claimed. No online hubs or search queue overflow leave the scheduled item queued rather than throwing.
behavior.completion: Timer checks and XML serialization are synchronous on callback thread; searches are dispatched through SearchManager and results are collected asynchronously.
behavior.cancellation: Expiry/removal is manager-owned; no caller cancellation token. Removing/disabling an expired item updates status and may remove it from the search collection.
persistence: Mutations set dirty and save after the second timer observes a 20-second interval. AutoSearch.xml persists groups, rule fields, params, finished paths and bundle tokens. Loading drops unresolved bundle tokens and disables expired rules with no associated bundle.
resources: TimerManager, SettingsManager XML, QueueManager listener/bundle lookup, ClientManager availability/queue overflow, shared AutoSearch lock and delayed-event queue.

ownership_evidence: AutoSearchManager owns the Search collection and listener lifecycle; loaded bundle references resolve to QueueManager-owned BundlePtr objects.
threading_evidence: Scheduler collection walks/mutations use AutoSearchManager SharedMutex; timer callbacks trigger search processing and save; addFailedBundle calls public add operation after duplicate/release checks.
records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Expose explicit expiry, time-window and persistence state; do not collapse due, disabled, expired, post-search and bundle-validation status. Preserve missing-field recovery and unresolved-bundle behavior.
acceptance_scenarios: Given an expired rule with no associated bundles, when REMOVE_EXPIRED_AS is enabled, then checkItems removes it; with the setting disabled and the item enabled, it disables it.
Given a saved rule without SearchDays/StartTime/EndTime/Target fields, when loading, then defaults are all weekdays, 00:00–23:59, and DOWNLOAD_DIRECTORY.
Given saved bundle tokens include one that no longer exists, when loading, then only extant QueueManager bundles are restored; an expired rule with no restored bundles is disabled.

Given a failed bundle name is a release and not already represented, when addFailedBundle is called, then a FAILED_BUNDLE rule is created with seven-day expiry and the configured failed-bundle group; non-release or duplicate names are rejected.
Given no online hubs or search queue overflow when a scheduled item becomes due, then maybePopSearchItem leaves it queued for a later callback.
records.mapping_note: Exact public scheduling/persistence/recovery operations and private timer/XML helpers are separated from add/remove and edit/group operations; behavior is source-traced and runtime module availability remains disabled/unverified.
